Treatment summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache
consistent with cervical strain. Over the course of twelve visits, care included physical examination, range-of-motion assessment,
a structured therapy program, and home exercise instruction. The reported injury is plausible given the mechanism of the
collision. Imaging and examination findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury to the cervical spine, with objective limitation in
motion and palpable muscle tightness. No prior injury to the neck or upper back is known from the patient's history. The course
of treatment followed a typical pattern, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms improved and range of motion returned
toward baseline. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no repeated or duplicate
entries. At the time of the final visit, the patient was discharged to self-directed home eexrcise with instructions to return if
symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any

- "reason": one short sentence.
